name: AARC Community Identity
description: Attributes to describe a user in the context of his community, as defined by AARC

attributes.name: voPersonId
attributes.description: A string representation of the subject’s identifier that is globally unique.

attributes.name: displayName
attributes.description: Subject’s full name in displayable form.

subAttributes.name: givenName
subAttributes.description: Name strings that are the part of a subject's name that is not their surname.

subAttributes.name: familyName
subAttributes.description: Surname(s) or last name(s) of the End-User.

attributes.name: email
attributes.description: The subject’s primary (preferred) email address for contact purposes. This email address must be formatted in Mailbox form as specified in RFC2821.

attributes.name: organizationName
attributes.description: Standard name of the organisation (institution) with which this subject is associated.

attributes.name: schacHomeOrganization
attributes.description: Specifies a subject’s home organisation using the domain name of the organisation according to [RFC1035].

attributes.name: voPersonExternalAffiliations
attributes.description: One or more home organisations (such as, universities, research institutions or private companies) that this subject is affiliated with. The syntax and semantics follows the eduPersonScopedAffiliation attribute.

subAttributes.name: value
subAttributes.description: Value of the voPersonExternalAffiliation. Example: gradstudent@yourvo.org

attributes.name: assurance
attributes.description: The assurance of the subject’s identity, following the components defined in the REFEDS Assurance Framework (RAF), including Identifier Uniqueness, Identity Assurance, and Attribute Assurance. AARC-compliant AAIs MAY also support additional assurance frameworks where relevant.

subAttributes.name: value
subAttributes.description: Value of the voPersonExternalAffiliation. Example: gradstudent@yourvo.org

attributes.name: entitlements
attributes.description: This attribute describes the groups and roles this subject is a member of (AARC-G069) or the resource or child-resource a subject is allowed to access, optionally specifying certain actions the subject is entitled to perform (AARC-G027).

attributes.name: entitlements
attributes.description: This attribute describes the groups and roles this subject is a member of (AARC-G069) or the resource or child-resource a subject is allowed to access, optionally specifying certain actions the subject is entitled to perform (AARC-G027).

attributes.name: Version
attributes.description: This attribute indicates the version of the AARC Attribute Profile that is being used. It provides a clear reference to the specific set of attributes and definitions that the subject’s digital identity conforms to.

attributes.name: voPersonScopedAffiliation
attributes.description: Specifies the person's affiliation within the Community/Research infrastructure in broad categories defined in the eduPerson schema. Any scope (e.g. “community.example.org”) used after the at sign MUST be announced by the Collaboration Management

attributes.name: AARCExternalIDs
attributes.description: External identifiers of the user (e.g. GitHub, Home Organisation identifier, gmail, etc)

attributes.name: eduPersonOrcid
attributes.description: ORCID identifier assigned to this user.

attributes.name: sshPublicKey
attributes.description: SSH public key(s) of the user.

attributes.name: voPersonCertificateDN
attributes.description: The Subject Distinguished Name(s) of the user's X.509 certificate(s).

attributes.name: voPersonCertificateIssuerDN
attributes.description: The Subject Distinguished Name(s) of the user’s X.509 certificate issuer(s).

attributes.name: UserType
attributes.description: This attribute indicates if the Community ID is a user ID or a service ID. A the Community user ID is a Community ID issued to a natural person who registers to the Collaboration Management. A Community service ID is a Community ID used by services which need to authenticate with other services. A Community service ID is owned by at least one Community user ID holder who is responsible for the service ID.
